ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Four cars drive into a roundabout at the same point in time, each one coming from a different direction (see diagram). No car drives all the way around the roundabout, and no two cars leave at the same exit. In how many different ways can the cars exit the roundabout?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circular roundabout, with four roads/exits connected around it, respectively located in the four directions of the roundabout; on each road there is one car entering the roundabout. The arrows inside the roundabout show the vehicles circling in the same direction. Reasoning: Label the four entrances/exits as 1, 2, 3, 4 according to the driving direction of the roundabout. The four cars enter from four different entrances respectively, and no two cars leave from the same exit, so the ways for the four cars to choose exits are a permutation of the four exits. Also because no car goes around a complete circle, any car cannot leave from the position the same as its own entrance, that is, the permutation cannot have a fixed point. Therefore one must count the number of derangements of 4 objects. Compute by inclusion-exclusion: 4! - C(4,1)3! + C(4,2)2! - C(4,3)1! + C(4,4)0! = 24 - 24 + 12 - 4 + 1 = 9.

raw_record.question_text: Four cars drive into a roundabout at the same point in time, each one coming from a different direction (see diagram). No car drives all the way around the roundabout, and no two cars leave at the same exit. In how many different ways can the cars exit the roundabout?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a four-exit roundabout: there are four approach roads/exits arranged around the circle, and exactly one car enters from each direction. Label the entry/exit positions 1, 2, 3, 4 around the roundabout in the traffic direction shown by the arrows. From the text, use that no two cars leave at the same exit, so the four cars collectively choose a permutation of the four exits. Also use that no car drives all the way around the roundabout, meaning a car may not leave at the same road position it entered after completing a full loop. Thus the task is to count permutations of four exits with no fixed points: a derangement of 4 objects. Compute by inclusion-exclusion: 4! - C(4,1)3! + C(4,2)2! - C(4,3)1! + C(4,4)0! = 24 - 24 + 12 - 4 + 1 = 9.
